overview: This Senate resolution names September 2026 as "National Cholesterol Education Month" and September 30, 2026, as "LDL-C Awareness Day." LDL-C is low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, often called "bad" cholesterol, which can build up in blood vessels and raise the risk of heart attacks and strokes. The resolution notes that heart disease is the leading cause of death in the United States and that many patients do not get recommended cholesterol tests, including after a hospital stay. It encourages everyone to know their LDL-C number and recognizes the need for screening and treatment. It does not create a program or spend money. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on September 28, 2026.
for: Supporters say raising awareness of cholesterol testing could help more people catch and treat a major, controllable risk factor for heart disease.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not fund screening or change health coverage, so its practical effect is limited.
